headline: Cursor links trojanized Claude Code extension on its marketplace to key stolen in Fireworks AI breach
summary: Cursor says an attacker used an access key issued to Fireworks AI, which was exposed in a breach at Fireworks. The incident ended with a trojanized version of the Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace. The full scope and number of affected users are not clear from the source.

headline: Cursor confirms breach enabled distribution of malicious Claude Code extension via its marketplace
summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach in which attackers distributed a malicious Claude Code extension through its extension marketplace. According to the report, the attackers got in using credentials stolen from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI. The source does not say how many users installed the extension or what it did.

headline: US disrupts North Korean 'FaceStealer' social engineering campaign tied to $400M crypto theft
summary: The US government says it has disrupted 'FaceStealer', a North Korean social engineering campaign blamed for stealing more than $400 million in cryptocurrency. The source does not detail the specific techniques used or who the victims were.

headline: Grafana Recorded Queries flaw (CVE-2026-12933) lets editors send requests to data source hosts
summary: CVE-2026-12933 is a flaw in Grafana. Its Recorded Queries remote-write endpoint tests connections with elevated credentials before checking whether the caller has permission. An attacker with organization editor rights could send authenticated requests to a data source host and infer sensitive data from the replies.

headline: Italian regulator fines Meta €805 million over Facebook Android gallery access
summary: Italy's data protection authority (Garante/GPDP) fined Meta €805 million. It found that a Facebook for Android feature accessed users' photos and videos without valid consent.

headline: Italy's Garante fines Meta €805M for default-on Facebook Android gallery access without consent
summary: The Garante found that a Facebook for Android photo-suggestion feature was switched on by default. It says the feature accessed Italian users' photos, videos and metadata without explicit consent. Meta reportedly has 60 days to respond or comply.

headline: GNU cpio through 2.15 has an out-of-bounds read when parsing newc/crc archive headers
summary: GNU cpio through version 2.15 has an out-of-bounds stack read in from_ascii() when it parses newc and crc archive headers. If the checksum field contains only spaces, the parser reads past the header buffer and may decode nearby stack bytes as header values. The Amazon Linux record does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: Italian authority fines Meta $887 million over Facebook access to Android gallery content
summary: An Italian authority fined Meta about $887 million over Facebook's access to photos and videos in Android device galleries. The authority said the relevant directive treats smartphones as part of a person's private sphere and requires free and informed consent for such access.

headline: Malvertising on Dutch news sites tried to infect iPhones with malware
summary: Attackers used the ad system on several Dutch websites, including VI, Autoblog and GeenStijl, to serve code that tried to infect iPhones with malware. The source does not say whether any devices were successfully compromised.

headline: Weekly recap: GitHub secret stealer and Claude Code abused as remote implant
summary: Help Net Security's weekly recap mentions a secret-stealing campaign against GitHub repositories and research on turning Claude Code into a remote-controlled implant. The source gives only brief detail.

headline: ESLint ends paid contributor program as AI-generated code strains open-source maintainers
summary: ESLint has ended its paid contributor program. Several open-source projects, including Rust, Godot and curl, are tightening contribution rules because AI-generated submissions are putting pressure on maintainers.

headline: Pentagon renames its Chief Digital and AI Office the 'Super Intelligence Office'
summary: SecurityWeek reports that the US Department of Defense has renamed its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO) the "Super Intelligence Office." The change follows a presidential order to say "super intelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence" in executive branch communications. The source does not describe any change to security requirements or operations.

headline: Opinion: Overreliance on AI may erode security teams' critical skills
summary: This SecurityWeek opinion piece argues that leaning too heavily on AI could weaken the creativity, communication and critical thinking that security teams need when no playbook applies. It reports no incident or vulnerability.

headline: datasette-llm 0.1a11 adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints and local models
summary: The datasette-llm plugin release 0.1a11 can now connect to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This lets Datasette Agent run with local models through tools such as LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp.

headline: Schneier lists upcoming November 2026 speaking engagements in Canada
summary: Bruce Schneier lists two upcoming talks, both in Ontario, Canada, on November 18 and 19, 2026. The post contains no security news.

headline: datasette-vega 0.7 charting plugin released with Datasette Lite support
summary: A new release of the datasette-vega charting plugin, its first since 2018, adds compatibility with the latest Datasette alphas and with Datasette Lite. The release has no security content.
